Formulation:  
Patrick Smith, a 35-year-old male lawyer, presents with new onset severe intermittent frontal headaches, palpitations, feeling hot, bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite with unintentional weight loss, and loss of libido coincident with recent job change. He has a known history of hyperthyroidism managed with thyroxine, adherent to medication. His symptoms are likely multifactorial with thyrotoxicosis or poor thyroid hormone control as the primary contributor, supported by palpitations, heat intolerance, and weight loss. Secondary psychological factors include significant occupational stress (7-8/10), which may exacerbate symptom presentation including headache and appetite changes, consistent with anxiety or stress-related syndrome. Bilateral hand tingling suggests possible peripheral neuropathy potentially related to thyroid dysfunction or nutritional deficits. Planned physical examination and thyroid function tests will clarify endocrine status and guide management. Psychological and occupational stressors appear to perpetuate symptoms. Protective factors and social supports are unreported.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Thyroid hormone imbalance (Hyperthyroidism/Thyrotoxicosis)  
- Patient Goal(s): Stabilize physical symptoms, improve energy and appetite, reduce palpitations and headaches  
- Clinical Goal(s): Optimize thyroid hormone control, exclude thyrotoxic crisis, and identify underlying causes of neurological symptoms  
- Actions (Patient): Attend scheduled in-person consultation for physical examination and blood testing; continue medication adherence; monitor symptoms  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Perform physical examination including cardiovascular and respiratory assessment; order thyroid function tests and other relevant labs; review thyroxine dosage; consider referral to endocrinology if indicated  

Secondary Problem: Anxiety/Stress-related syndrome  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce stress and improve coping during work; improve mood and libido  
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify and manage stress-related symptoms to alleviate psychological and somatic complaints  
- Actions (Patient): Engage in stress management strategies; discuss work-related stressors; consider self-help or counseling options if symptoms persist  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Screen for anxiety and depressive symptoms on follow-up; provide psychoeducation; consider referral for psychological therapies as needed

- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Explanation of symptoms possibly related to thyroid hormone imbalance and stress; importance of medication adherence; symptom monitoring and reporting; appointment for physical examination and labs  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased palpitations, worsening headache severity or frequency, new neurological deficits, significant mood changes, suicidal ideation  
- Coping Strategies: Stress reduction at work, relaxation techniques (not explicitly documented but implied as part of clinician advice for stress management)

  Justification: Known hyperthyroidism on thyroxine; symptoms of palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss, new headaches, and neuropathic symptoms consistent with thyrotoxicosis or thyroid dysfunction.  
- Anxiety/Stress-related syndrome – Medium likelihood
